html:
SMTO-FIL-0026 — SMTO can only work with ordinary files here

GUID: ac7e5116-3688-46f6-a487-5eace3ad03bc
Slug: file-special-file-unsupported
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • The location points to a special system item, not an ordinary file. Examples are a device, a pipe, a shortcut-style link or a special Windows link. SMTO's file actions can't read, copy or send it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the location in Technical details. If you meant an ordinary file, tell SMTO that file's exact name and location. SMTO can read and copy ordinary files, but not the special item it reached.
  2. If the item is a link or shortcut to a file, tell SMTO the location of the real file it points to. Using the real file avoids the link, which SMTO won't open as content.
  3. If a folder you're copying contains special items, ask SMTO to copy only the ordinary files and folders in it. Folder copies stop when they reach an item type they can't copy.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reads, copies or transfers the ordinary file and the step completes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway's computer. Don't treat the special item as copied or read; SMTO did not handle it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway file content operation or transfer reached a non-regular resource (device, FIFO, socket, unfollowed symlink, Windows reparse point or other special type), or a recursive copy met a type other than regular file, directory or symlink.

What this means

  • A regular-file boundary received a device, FIFO, socket, reparse point or other unsupported resource type; recursive copy permits only its explicit type set. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A regular-file boundary received a device, FIFO, socket, reparse point or other unsupported resource type; recursive copy permits only its explicit type set.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the resource type without reading from an unbounded device or following unsupported links.

How to fix it

  • Check the type fact in the receipt and lstat the path on the Gateway. Target the regular file instead (set follow_symlinks=true when a link's target is intended), exclude special entries from recursive copies, or use a purpose-built capability for devices, sockets or pipes (gateway_core/file_common.regular, file_manage.copy, transfer.TransferProvider._open).
  • Use a regular file or a supported system capability appropriate to this resource.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported resource type is selected for the intended capability.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
